course.title: Craves engineering laboratories: trace, extend, test and recover every service
course.description: Nine practical laboratories connect the original service courses to implementation evidence. Each requires source tracing, explicit acceptance cases, a safe local exercise, a review packet and recovery reasoning. Quiz completion does not certify an unreviewed code change or grant production access.

lessons.title: Authentication lab: establish, renew, revoke and verify the correct identity
lessons.overview: This lab follows the Auth service from a verified external identity to Craves claims, an administrator session and downstream access. The service is an especially sensitive deployment boundary because customers, chefs and administrators depend on it. Begin by separating identity verification from role assignment, a consumer session from an internal administrator family, and a successful token refresh from permission to perform a business action. Read AuthController, AuthService, AdminSessionService, CravesJwtAuthenticationFilter and InternalAdminRoles at the pinned source revision. Course content must never be used to justify granting a role or fabricating a token for a production smoke test.

steps.label: Draw the trust chain
steps.detail: Start at the exchange endpoint in AuthController and follow the actual service verification, user mapping and token issuance. Record the source of identity, phone and role claims and where external credentials are verified. Then trace a protected request through the JWT filter to the controller principal. Do not assume a decoded JWT is verified merely because its payload can be read.

steps.label: Separate the session policies
steps.detail: Read AdminSessionService and the policy tests. The reviewed internal policy has an original eight-hour absolute boundary and shorter access tokens; ordinary consumer/chef flows retain their separate policy. Renewal must not move an absolute family deadline. A staff identity entering a consumer flow must not acquire internal administrative privileges from a frontend selection.

steps.label: Model concurrency and revocation
steps.detail: Write expected behavior for concurrent refresh, replay of a rotated credential, logout racing refresh and an account whose role or session is revoked. Identify which behavior is enforced by the database/session family and which is only coordinated in the browser. A successful fresh token is not proof that all downstream services check live revocation.

steps.label: Run focused baseline tests
steps.detail: From the repository root run mvn -B -f services/auth-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AdminSessionPolicyTest,InternalAdminRolesTest test. Inspect the PostgreSQL session test setup and its required disposable database variables before running AdminSessionPersistenceTest. Record conditional skips separately; do not point that suite to the Auth production database.

steps.label: Design an approved-style extension
steps.detail: For a local training exercise, propose an additional read-only administrative capability. Document the exact permitted roles, source principal, response fields, revoked-session behavior and privacy boundary. Add tests before changing the local controller or policy. Do not broaden the shared JWT filter or introduce a generic ADMIN role to make one feature accessible.

steps.label: Prepare failure-safe release evidence
steps.detail: List the exact Auth files that changed, all consumers affected, expected old/new token behavior and rollback compatibility. A real release must preserve issuer, audience, secret references, replica limits and downstream routes. Include anonymous denial, consumer denial, legitimate administrator access and post-revocation denial. Controlled-clock tests and a real eight-hour browser observation are distinct evidence.

lessons.example: A user signs out while another tab is refreshing. The late refresh response must not restore protected UI or a session that has been revoked. Test both the browser state guard and the server family/replay behavior rather than assuming one covers the other.
lessons.lab: Submit a sequence diagram for exchange, protected read, refresh and logout; a role matrix using the actual nine internal roles; and a test matrix for wrong signature, expiry, wrong role, replay and logout/refresh races. Run the focused tests and the approved disposable persistence suite, attach sanitized reports and identify every unexecuted live case. A peer must explain which credentials are external, which are Craves-issued and which operation revokes the family. Do not send OTPs, rotate signing keys or log in as a real administrator as part of this local lab.
lessons.pitfall: Passing an authentication test is not permission to weaken production authorization, and simulated time is not a completed browser soak.

questions.prompt: What must not change when an absolute administrator session is renewed?
questions.explanation: Renewal cannot indefinitely extend an absolute session family lifetime.

questions.prompt: Does reading a JWT payload verify its authenticity?
options: Yes, if it contains a phone number
No; signature and the required claims must be verified
Yes, if the user is staff
questions.explanation: Decoding is not cryptographic verification or authorization.

questions.prompt: Which evidence proves a real eight-hour browser observation?
options: An actually observed, recorded browser session across that boundary
questions.explanation: Time-simulated tests and a real browser soak are different kinds of evidence.

lessons.title: People lab: customer, chef and administrator data without privacy leakage
lessons.overview: User-Chef owns customer/chef profile facts, saved addresses and chef onboarding state. An administrator directory is a controlled investigative view over that data, not unrestricted access to every table. The reviewed AdminDirectoryController requires an X-Admin-Reason and returns no-store responses with X-Correlation-ID. AdminDirectoryService owns the actual validation, permission and response construction. This lab teaches how to extend a legitimate profile or administrative read without trusting a client-selected owner, exposing sensitive fields or rewriting historical order snapshots after a profile change.

steps.label: Map the user and chef identities
steps.detail: Read the service README and locate the relevant profile/address/chef controllers. Distinguish an authentication identity from customer and chef domain records and from approval status. One person may participate in more than one role, but each request still requires the correct authorization and lifecycle state. Do not infer chef approval merely from a selected UI mode.

steps.label: Trace the directory entry point
steps.detail: POST /api/v1/admin/directory/search passes the verified CurrentUser, query and reason to the service. Customer and chef case reads also require the reason header. Follow the service rather than assuming the controller's presence establishes every permission. Map request validation, audit/correlation generation and the resulting public administrative DTO.

steps.label: Classify fields before adding them
steps.detail: For a proposed new field, record owner, sensitivity, write authority, read roles, null behavior and retention. A display preference differs from a payment credential or identity document. Do not add secret material or full customer payloads to a broad directory response to simplify debugging.

steps.label: Preserve historical boundaries
steps.detail: An address edit changes the profile's current address record, not a completed checkout's saved delivery snapshot. A new profile feature used during checkout needs an explicit Order contract and snapshot decision. Test profile updates after order creation to distinguish current profile facts from historical order facts.

steps.label: Build and test a local vertical slice
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/user-chef-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AdminDirectoryServiceTest test before editing. For a hypothetical local display-preference extension, plan DTO, service validation, persistence if needed, ownership tests and a narrow web adapter. This is a training requirement, not an already approved production profile field.

steps.label: Review the administrative evidence
steps.detail: Test missing or invalid reason, wrong role, a customer attempting the admin route, unknown identity and deliberately cross-owner inputs. Verify response fields and no-store headers through the actual route in a non-production environment. Keep reason/correlation data useful without putting raw personal information into public screenshots or issue comments.

lessons.example: An administrator investigates a chef case with a legitimate reason. A support-friendly response may expose relevant approved fields, but it must not expose all stored identity documents or credentials simply because the administrator can read the directory.
lessons.lab: Create a data ownership diagram and an administrative access matrix. Trace one customer case and one chef case through controller, service and response DTO. Run AdminDirectoryServiceTest, then add local negative cases for missing reason, unsupported role and forbidden field disclosure. Produce a proposed feature file plan and a before/after snapshot test for an address edit. A peer must be able to identify the permitted reader of every new field and explain why existing orders remain unchanged.
lessons.pitfall: Administrative visibility is not unlimited database ownership. Do not widen a shared response or rewrite historical addresses to fix a display problem.

questions.prompt: Which header carries the inspected directory investigation reason?
questions.explanation: The actual directory controller accepts X-Admin-Reason and passes it to the service.

questions.prompt: Should editing a saved customer address rewrite an old order's snapshot?
options: Yes, every address must match today's value
No; historical order facts remain owned by Order
Only if the order has two kitchens
questions.explanation: Current profile data and historical checkout snapshots have different ownership and meaning.

questions.prompt: What must precede adding a field to an administrator directory response?
options: A decision about sensitivity and authorized readers
questions.explanation: Response expansion needs an explicit privacy and role boundary.

lessons.title: Catalog lab: implement a discoverable field across write, read, filter and cache paths
lessons.overview: A catalog change is incomplete when a chef can save a field but customers cannot discover or interpret it consistently. Trace the write DTO and CatalogService, persistence, public response, nearby search criteria, cache key, browser/mobile parser and rendered states. Keep commercial and food-safety semantics owned by the product rather than inferring them from a field name. This laboratory uses an approved-style optional display attribute as a local exercise; it does not create nutritional, allergen, pricing or compliance claims. The separate Data Engineering course explains the spatial and cache mechanics in detail.

steps.label: Define the field contract
steps.detail: State whether the proposed attribute is optional, its accepted values, length, owner and visibility. Explain old-row behavior and whether it affects filtering or sorting. An optional display attribute should not silently change order eligibility, commission or pricing. Record any unresolved product decision before writing implementation code.

steps.label: Trace the write boundary
steps.detail: Locate the real chef/menu write path and its service authorization. Check that the authenticated chef owns the relevant kitchen before mutation. Follow the DTO into CatalogService and persistence, identify transactional behavior and preserve validation for package and availability facts. Do not assume a valid kitchen UUID establishes ownership.

steps.label: Trace the public boundary
steps.detail: Follow PublicCatalogController and NearbyDiscoveryController to their DTOs. Explicitly choose which fields are public. Test unavailable or inactive items, missing optional data and existing records written before the extension. Keep internal moderation or operational metadata out of public responses.

steps.label: Connect discovery semantics
steps.detail: If the approved requirement adds a filter, update request validation, SQL criteria and cache identity together. Use longitude/latitude and meter-based radius as implemented. A nearby match is not delivery-provider serviceability approval. Exercise page boundaries and multiple filter combinations with synthetic data.

steps.label: Run targeted source checks
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/catalog-service/pom.xml -Dtest=NearbyDiscoveryServiceValidationTest,NearbyDiscoveryServiceCriteriaValidationTest test. Read what those validation tests actually cover; add database, cache and ownership coverage where the proposed change needs it. Do not represent a criteria-only unit test as proof of SQL query plans or production Redis invalidation.

steps.label: Complete consumer compatibility
steps.detail: Update strict web/mobile parsing and UI fallback for the new optional value. Test an older response without it and an invalid response containing the wrong type. Record precise changed paths and rollback behavior, including whether older service versions ignore the additive database field. Leave cache enablement and live Catalog flags untouched in this lab.

lessons.example: A new filter produces correct uncached results but is omitted from the cache key. Two customers using different filters can receive the same cached list. A complete feature test includes cached and uncached request separation, not just a controller success.
lessons.lab: Prepare a local patch plan for an optional catalog display attribute. Include field definition, write authorization, migration if needed, public DTO, discovery criteria when approved, cache key, parser and UI states. Run the baseline criteria tests and create a synthetic table of old rows, new rows, unavailable items, wrong owner and malformed filter. A reviewer must reproduce expected results and identify any unexecuted database/cache evidence. Do not change a production menu, price, radius or dietary claim to demonstrate the exercise.
lessons.pitfall: Changing only the UI or only the write DTO creates a half-implemented feature. Every dependent read, filter, cache and parser must be considered.

questions.prompt: A new filter affects results. Which additional component must reflect it?
options: The cache key and query contract
questions.explanation: The cache and database query must distinguish requests whose results differ.

questions.prompt: What does a nearby Catalog match not prove?
options: That a query returned a result
That a response can be parsed
That an item has an identifier
questions.explanation: Geographic discovery and operational provider eligibility are distinct contracts.

questions.prompt: How should old responses without a newly optional field be handled?
options: Assume every old client is upgraded
Use the documented compatible parser/UI fallback
questions.explanation: Additive features need backward-compatible behavior for old rows and responses.

lessons.title: Order lab: follow the real checkout entry point and prove one coherent order graph
lessons.overview: The actual creation entry point is CheckoutController at /api/v1/checkout, which calls OrderService.checkout. OrderController at /api/v1/orders reads existing orders; it does not create checkout. ChefOrderController owns chef-facing action routes such as accept, reject and ready-for-pickup. Trace these concrete paths before modifying the order lifecycle. A multi-kitchen checkout contains a parent checkout and independently progressing kitchen orders. Order owns saved facts and transitions, while Catalog and User-Chef supply current lookup facts and Integration owns external payment/delivery execution. This lab does not invent cancellation, refund or preparation rules.

steps.label: Trace request to saved graph
steps.detail: Start at CheckoutController's POST method, identify the verified CurrentUser and CheckoutRequest, then step through OrderService.checkout. Record address/menu lookups, the grouping by kitchen, allocated identifiers, persisted snapshots and any receipt or duplicate check. Use a two-kitchen fixture so a parent/child mix-up is visible.

steps.label: Map historical data precisely
steps.detail: List item, price, pickup, drop-off and package facts captured at checkout. Distinguish a saved snapshot from a mutable foreign reference. Inspect CheckoutSnapshotFactory and its tests rather than assuming every field is copied. A later kitchen/profile edit must not rewrite a previously accepted order's historical facts.

steps.label: Write the transition table
steps.detail: For each chef action, record allowed prior state, resulting state, required actor, timestamp and downstream effect. Derive the table from the inspected service implementation and approved functional specification. Mark gaps rather than inventing a new refund outcome. Test repeated, conflicting and concurrent actions explicitly.

steps.label: Separate local and external commitments
steps.detail: Find the order-domain outbox/event path and identify the local transaction boundary. A request can commit before a downstream notification or delivery action completes. Define how an operator sees pending downstream work and reconciles it without creating a second order or overriding a payment status.

steps.label: Run focused and integrated tests
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/order-service/pom.xml -Dtest=CheckoutSnapshotFactoryTest test for the snapshot baseline. That test alone does not prove full checkout SQL, dependency failures or chef concurrency. Add or execute relevant disposable integration tests for the actual change and record exactly what ran, including database conditions and skipped suites.

steps.label: Design recovery before rollout
steps.detail: For a hypothetical additive order metadata feature, ensure older code can read rows written by the new version. Record a prior healthy image and avoid destructive rollback migrations. A real release must verify routed authorization, exact saved state and downstream correlation, not only /actuator/health. No real charge or delivery is necessary for this local lab.

lessons.example: The first kitchen accepts while the second has not responded. Showing the entire checkout as identically progressed can mislead customers and downstream dispatch. Inspect parent and child state separately and verify the actual aggregation contract.
lessons.lab: Create a two-kitchen checkout sequence diagram and persisted-state matrix covering valid checkout, unavailable required lookup, repeated submit, later profile edit, one chef acceptance, one conflicting action and a repeated downstream signal. Record allowed behavior from source and flag any policy question. Run the snapshot test and relevant isolated integration coverage. Submit a local-only additive feature plan with complete path mapping, negative cases and backward-compatible recovery. The peer review must explain why OrderController is not the checkout creation entry point.
lessons.pitfall: Do not repair a workflow by manually setting an order to PAID, deleting evidence or recreating an uncertain delivery booking.

questions.prompt: Which controller calls the reviewed OrderService.checkout method?
questions.explanation: CheckoutController handles POST /api/v1/checkout; OrderController reads existing orders.

questions.prompt: Why use a two-kitchen fixture?
options: To expose parent/child ownership and independent progression mistakes
questions.explanation: A multi-kitchen fixture reveals errors hidden by single-order happy paths.

questions.prompt: What should remain unchanged after a later profile edit?
questions.explanation: Historical checkout facts remain stable even when mutable source records change.

lessons.title: Payment lab: reconcile provider evidence without duplicate financial effects
lessons.overview: Payment creation, provider authorization, capture, webhook receipt and the Craves paid state are distinct events. PaymentController exposes create, read, verify and provider webhook routes, while PaymentService owns the orchestration. The repository contains both Cashfree and Razorpay paths; a class existing in source does not prove which one is live. This lab must preserve the currently approved runtime provider and never switch credentials or create a real transaction. The engineering goal is to prove amount/currency/ownership binding, authenticated provider evidence, replay handling and safe recovery from an uncertain response.

steps.label: Trace creation preconditions
steps.detail: Read POST /api/v1/payments/orders. It checks order-execution enablement and the scheduled-payment eligibility guard before calling PaymentService.createPaymentOrder with Authorization and the DTO. Inspect the service's ownership and authoritative checkout lookup. Do not accept a browser-supplied display total as an independent source of payable money.

steps.label: Separate UI acknowledgment from truth
steps.detail: A payment popup success or callback is not a substitute for backend/provider verification. Trace /orders/{paymentOrderId}/verify and the provider-specific client. Write which provider order and payment identifiers are compared, which amount and currency are authoritative and how Craves records a verified terminal result.

steps.label: Inspect webhook entry points
steps.detail: PaymentController forwards Cashfree's timestamp/signature/version/idempotency headers and raw body to its inbox service, while the Razorpay route forwards signature, event ID and raw body to PaymentService. These headers differ; do not normalize the body before verifying a signature or substitute one provider's contract for another.

steps.label: Enumerate failure windows
steps.detail: Test provider-create timeout, verification unavailable, invalid signature, duplicate event, out-of-order event, wrong amount/currency and a payment reference belonging to another owner. Define the expected durable state and reconciliation action for each. A timeout must not cause another financial order to be created blindly.

steps.label: Run safe baseline tests
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/integration-service/pom.xml -Dtest=PaymentOwnershipGuardTest,PaymentApiPropertiesTest,PaymentProviderPropertiesTest,ScheduledPaymentEligibilityGuardTest test. These are focused tests, not a live captured-payment test. For any extended behavior, add provider mocks and disposable persistence cases at the actual mutation boundary.

steps.label: Prepare an auditable extension
steps.detail: For a local status-display enhancement, carry typed canonical backend states and correlation evidence into the web/mobile client without initiating new payments. A production change to provider routing, fees, refund policy or credentials requires separate owner approval. Retain the original payment/order/webhook evidence through rollback and never print keys or raw payment payloads in public training output.

lessons.example: The provider captured a payment, but the verification response to the browser was lost. Creating another payment order risks double charging. Reconcile the existing owned payment reference and its provider/webhook evidence before any new action.
lessons.lab: Produce a payment evidence table connecting checkout ID, payment-order ID, provider order/payment reference, verified event, canonical state and downstream order effect using synthetic values. Run the focused baseline tests and create mock cases for invalid signature, duplicate webhook, amount mismatch and an uncertain create response. Verify that one accepted event does not produce repeated paid transitions. Mark live payment, key rotation and provider activation NOT EXECUTED. A peer must explain why a green checkout popup is insufficient proof.
lessons.pitfall: Never perform repeated live charges to diagnose a training or dashboard issue. Preserve uncertain outcomes and reconcile the original references.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is insufficient by itself to mark Craves paid?
options: An authenticated provider result bound to the correct order
A valid verified webhook handled by the backend
questions.explanation: Client UI success is not authoritative financial verification.

questions.prompt: How should a lost provider-create response be handled?
options: Reconcile the existing owned request/reference before retrying effects
questions.explanation: The provider may have accepted the first request; a blind new operation risks duplication.

questions.prompt: Does a Cashfree or Razorpay class in source establish that provider is active now?
options: No; activation requires current runtime evidence
questions.explanation: Source capability, configuration and production acceptance are distinct.

lessons.title: Delivery lab: connect provider eligibility, assignment, outcomes and history
lessons.overview: Delivery Intelligence ranks eligible inputs and records an assignment; it is not proof that a rider was actually booked or completed a delivery. The reviewed service checks feature enablement, existing chef-suborder assignment, provider activity, area membership and input availability. It combines predictor output, rolling metrics, exploration and proximity using configured weights. Those mathematical scores must remain separate from production provider readiness and real outcome evidence. Craves requires approved hyperlocal behavior; do not activate a standard parcel API or invent selection economics while building a training example.

steps.label: Trace eligibility before ranking
steps.detail: Follow assign to its existing-assignment lookup and createAssignment. Ineligible providers are skipped before scoring. Read the code's treatment of empty service-area lists precisely; it accepts them at this layer, so the caller/provider readiness boundary must not be assumed from this predicate alone. A registration row is not commercial or production API approval.

steps.label: Explain each score input
steps.detail: Identify DeliverySuccessPredictor, PartnerMetrics, BetaSampler and the configured quality/proximity weights. Separate an observed metric from a prior or heuristic. The deterministic seed used for a request assists reproducibility; it does not establish model calibration, fairness or guaranteed rider availability. Do not claim accuracy figures without measured evaluation data.

steps.label: Trace assignment to external work
steps.detail: Locate the delivery command/adapter and provider-create path in the repository, then connect its identifiers to the chef-specific order and assignment. Mark the point where an external request can create a real booking. An uncertain response after that boundary requires provider reconciliation, not automatic failover that might dispatch two riders.

steps.label: Trace normalized outcomes
steps.detail: recordOutcome validates the provider and delegates scoring and insert-if-absent persistence. Inspect the concrete uniqueness and source-event identity before claiming replay safety. Test duplicate and late terminal events, timestamp semantics and missing fields. Synthetic fixtures must not be inserted into production model feedback or live provider statistics.

steps.label: Validate historical visibility
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/integration-service/pom.xml -Dtest=DeliveryIntelligenceNeutralProximityTest,DeliveryIntelligenceHistoryReadRepositoryTest,AdminDeliveryIntelligenceHistoryControllerTest test. Check database conditions and skipped cases. Test recent and older records, supported filters, pagination and empty ranges. A first-page response must not be labeled the complete all-time history.

steps.label: Design a safe feature extension
steps.detail: For a local explanation-panel enhancement, expose only reviewed score components and source timestamps under proper administrator authorization. Keep provider credentials, customer addresses and raw payloads out of broad analytics. Preserve current provider flags, weights, callback routes and one-replica limits; this lab cannot activate a vendor or certify huge-load behavior.

lessons.example: A top-ranked provider may have a valid score but no approved production-create binding. The UI must distinguish ranked, eligible, booking requested, provider accepted, rider assigned and delivered evidence rather than using one green badge for everything.
lessons.lab: Create a synthetic assignment with one inactive provider, one unavailable candidate and two eligible candidates. Trace the recorded score components and deterministic ordering, then replay the same chef-suborder assignment and inspect the actual persistence behavior. Draw the separate provider booking and status reconciliation chain. Produce a history matrix with old/new records, date boundaries, provider filters and pagination. A reviewer must identify where duplicate rider creation is prevented and what remains unproven by ranking tests. Do not call any real delivery provider or send synthetic outcomes to production.
lessons.pitfall: A model recommendation is not a live dispatch confirmation, and a provider dashboard account is not proof of an approved hyperlocal API integration.

questions.prompt: What must be established before a candidate's high score is operationally useful?
options: Its production eligibility and the correct executable provider path
questions.explanation: Ranking cannot replace readiness, serviceability and an approved provider integration.

questions.prompt: Why avoid blind provider failover after an uncertain booking response?
options: The first provider may already have created a booking
questions.explanation: Uncertain external creation can lead to duplicate riders unless reconciled first.

questions.prompt: What does a page of recent history not establish?
options: That the route can produce a response
That all older records and filters are correctly represented
questions.explanation: Complete historical visibility requires pagination and boundary/filter evidence.

lessons.title: Subscription lab: keep schedules, billing and fulfilment distinct
lessons.overview: A subscription plan, its meal schedule, a customer's subscription, a billing invoice and each fulfilment occurrence are different domain objects. A recurring schedule is not proof of payment or authority to create an unlimited set of orders. The reviewed PlanScheduleService publishes only active-plan schedules and protects administrative reads with PLATFORM_ADMIN or SUBSCRIPTION_ADMIN. This read service does not establish the entire billing or occurrence-generation contract. The lab follows those adjacent modules explicitly, identifies their enablement and replay boundaries and leaves lead times, capacity, cancellation and refund policies with the product owner.

steps.label: Draw the lifecycle entities
steps.detail: Use the Subscription README to locate plan, schedule, subscription, invoice/payment intent and occurrence/fulfilment modules. Record each identifier, owner and status. Avoid calling all of them an order. Identify the event or command that crosses from Subscription into Order and the durable reference that links them.

steps.label: Read public versus admin schedule behavior
steps.detail: getPublicActive requires an ACTIVE plan and an active schedule, then constructs a public projection of schedule items. The administrative get path requires the two actual permitted roles. Test inactive or unknown plans and inspect which internal fields are deliberately absent from the public response.

steps.label: Define time semantics without guessing policy
steps.detail: Record recurrence type, timezone, day/slot fields and the implemented validation. Convert a synthetic service date to its intended instant and test month boundaries and invalid combinations. Do not invent a production lead time, maximum horizon or capacity number to fill a missing functional-spec decision.

steps.label: Trace payment eligibility separately
steps.detail: Locate invoice/payment-intent creation and the payment-status consumer. A schedule existing does not mean its invoice is PAID, and a created payment intent is not a captured payment. Follow the exact owned references and replay checks before allowing downstream fulfilment in a proposed feature.

steps.label: Test occurrence replay and capacity
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/subscription-service/pom.xml -Dtest=PlanScheduleRequestValidationTest test as a validation baseline. Then inspect the occurrence and fulfilment tests applicable to your change. Simulate a worker restart and repeated event using a disposable database; verify the actual occurrence uniqueness and capacity behavior rather than assuming the schedule read test proves it.

steps.label: Complete a reversible feature plan
steps.detail: For a local schedule-display extension, define additive DTO and parser behavior while keeping existing commercial rules unchanged. If a change affects generated future occurrences or billing, document the migration and rollback implications explicitly. Do not enable dormant subscription workers, create production policy rows or run catch-up generation to demonstrate the lab.

lessons.example: A customer's plan display can be correct while an invoice remains unpaid or a future occurrence has not been generated. A dashboard should present these as separate states, with the actual source references and timestamps, rather than claiming fulfilment is ready.
lessons.lab: Build a lifecycle table for one synthetic plan and two service dates: schedule availability, subscription state, invoice state, payment reference, occurrence ID and order reference. Run the validation baseline, then demonstrate a repeated occurrence-generation input in isolated tests. Include inactive plan, wrong administrative role, invalid timezone/day combination, unpaid invoice and repeated payment-status event. Mark every policy parameter as sourced or pending approval. A peer must explain how one restart cannot silently generate duplicate fulfilment orders under the implemented contract.
lessons.pitfall: Do not infer billing or fulfilment readiness from an active plan alone, and do not seed commercial policy just to make a scheduler run.

questions.prompt: Which roles can perform the reviewed administrative schedule read?
questions.explanation: PlanScheduleService explicitly checks those two administrative roles.

questions.prompt: What does an active schedule not prove?
options: That its read contract can return items
That the relevant customer invoice is paid
questions.explanation: Scheduling, billing and payment are separate lifecycle facts.

questions.prompt: How should an unspecified production lead-time rule be handled?
options: Keep it an explicit product decision rather than inventing a value
Hide it in a UI constant
questions.explanation: Engineering cannot silently create scheduling policy.

lessons.title: Notification lab: requests, preferences, devices and recovery evidence
lessons.overview: Notification requests, an in-app inbox, registered push devices, channel preferences and external delivery outcomes are separate concerns. NotificationDeliveryController registers ANDROID or IOS devices, scopes records to the verified identity and supports the reviewed IN_APP, PUSH and EMAIL preference channels. InternalNotificationController is a separate service-to-service entry point. Read each path's authorization and durable state rather than assuming one endpoint covers them all. A provider acceptance response is not proof that a person saw a message, and a quiet queue is not proof that a worker is enabled or progressing.

steps.label: Map the delivery chain
steps.detail: Start with an owning domain event or internal request, then identify deduplication, saved notification/inbox data, channel eligibility, worker attempt and provider outcome. Record correlation fields and terminal/retryable states from the actual implementation. Do not use a course exercise to send notifications to real customers.

steps.label: Trace device ownership
steps.detail: The delivery controller derives the identity from Authentication and normalizes the platform to ANDROID or IOS. Device registration, listing and deactivation call the repository with that identity. Test that a device identifier from another account cannot be deactivated or exposed by a caller who merely knows its UUID.

steps.label: Read preferences precisely
steps.detail: The reviewed preference route normalizes and allowlists IN_APP, PUSH and EMAIL. Do not add SMS or WhatsApp as a working preference solely because another module or product plan mentions them. Changing mandatory transactional versus optional messaging behavior needs an approved consent/product rule and tests in the actual delivery path.

steps.label: Handle retries and unknown outcomes
steps.detail: Inspect each channel worker and gateway before classifying a failure. A definitely rejected preflight differs from a timeout after an external send. Preserve the original request identity and provider evidence. Document-specific UNKNOWN email handling is covered by the PDF course and must not be casually replaced with bulk retries.

steps.label: Run the focused persistence baseline
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -f services/notification-service/pom.xml -Dtest=NotificationDeliveryRepositoryTest,NotificationDeliveryPropertiesTest test in the environment required by those tests. Inspect conditional database requirements and actual executed counts. Add two-owner fixtures and provider mocks for a proposed preference/device change; a property-validation test alone does not prove delivery.

steps.label: Plan operations and rollback
steps.detail: Measure pending age, retries, terminal failures and successful worker progress. A recovery action should target an approved set of requests, preserve evidence and avoid sending duplicates. Keep document, general notification and channel flags distinct. A real release must not disable working channels or change recipient resolution to make one new feature appear successful.

lessons.example: A user disables an optional channel preference while a request is queued. The expected delivery behavior must be defined by the actual approved contract and tested at the point where eligibility is evaluated; it cannot be guessed from the toggle's appearance.
lessons.lab: Create two synthetic identities and a device/preference test matrix: valid Android registration, valid iOS registration, unsupported platform, unsupported channel, another owner's device, repeated request and provider timeout. Trace one internal notification to its durable delivery evidence. Run the focused suites and explain all skips. For a local extension, provide the exact DTO/repository/controller/client paths and state which consent or delivery decisions require approval. Do not perform bulk replays or send a real email, SMS or push message.
lessons.pitfall: Do not equate provider acceptance with recipient attention, or assume all channels and recovery flags share one lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Which preference channels are allowlisted by the reviewed controller?
questions.explanation: The inspected controller explicitly declares these three channels.

questions.prompt: How is ownership applied to device deactivation?
options: Through the verified identity passed to the repository
questions.explanation: The endpoint must remain scoped to the caller's authenticated identity.

questions.prompt: What can a zero-length queue fail to reveal?
options: Whether workers are enabled and making meaningful progress
questions.explanation: Queue length alone is not sufficient worker-health or delivery evidence.

lessons.title: Web and release lab: build a complete protected feature and prove its routed version
lessons.overview: The Next.js backend-for-frontend adapts browser sessions and controlled routes to Java APIs; it does not become a second business backend. server-api.ts obtains the existing HttpOnly access cookie, validates the requested relative path, performs live administrative identity verification for the relevant routes and sends bounded no-store upstream requests. Academy demonstrates why source publication, CI, image deployment, gateway routing and authenticated browser acceptance must be recorded separately. Its lesson files are classpath resources in Auth's image, so a Git merge alone cannot update the courses seen by an administrator.

steps.label: Map all route layers
steps.detail: For Academy write down browser /api/admin/academy/catalog, gateway /academy/catalog and Java /api/v1/admin/academy/catalog. Read api-target.ts rather than concatenating /api/v1 with /academy blindly. Existing non-Academy routes keep their normal base. A route fix must not rewrite other APIs while solving the Academy path.

steps.label: Trace session and status handling
steps.detail: The shared server adapter reads the access cookie and verifies administrative identity before protected upstream work. The Academy BFF allowlists methods and paths, bounds bodies and maps allowed statuses. A frontend control must not bypass server role checks. A 401, a forbidden role, a temporary upstream outage and malformed JSON need distinct handling where the contract allows it.

steps.label: Implement all interaction states
steps.detail: For a hypothetical protected read panel, build loading, ready, empty, forbidden, signed-out and reconnect states. Keep in-progress input during a temporary reconnect, but clear protected data on terminal logout. Test stale responses after navigation and role changes. Use semantic controls, keyboard focus and readable text rather than relying on visual success alone.

steps.label: Run actual web gates
steps.detail: From apps/customer-web-next run npm ci, node --test --experimental-strip-types src/lib/academy-*.test.ts, npm run typecheck and npm run build; use the checked-in Academy workflow's lint command. Record the real test totals and artifact source. Passing TypeScript does not validate every upstream runtime object or demonstrate a signed-in production journey.

steps.label: Prove a narrow publication
steps.detail: For a curriculum-only change, compare the Auth source/image and returned catalog version. The generic existing UI consumes returned courses, so do not redeploy customer, payment, delivery or other backends just to refresh lesson resources. A live release needs an authorized deployment connection, a known healthy rollback image, preserved settings and a catalog read through the actual administrator route.

steps.label: Close with honest evidence
steps.detail: Record source commit, CI runs, immutable image digest, latest/ready revision, unchanged one-replica limits, feature flag and authenticated catalog counts. If Azure login fails or no authenticated browser session is available, mark those gates blocked rather than saying published. A successful anonymous denial proves protection, not that the administrator can see the new curriculum.

lessons.example: The repository contains version v3 while the browser receives v1. The next diagnostic is the deployed Auth image and routed catalog version, not a full seven-service redeployment or deletion of learner progress.
lessons.lab: Prepare a complete local read-panel implementation plan using the real BFF and component paths. Test unknown routes, wrong methods, malformed upstream JSON, expired session, temporary outage, stale response and keyboard navigation. Then build a release evidence sheet with source/CI/image/revision/route/catalog version and explicit PASS, FAIL or NOT EXECUTED statuses. A peer must identify the one remaining gate when source is merged but the image is still old. Do not claim LIVE unless the production publication and authorized routed result have actually been checked.
lessons.pitfall: Do not confuse a source-control milestone with a live publication, or use an unrelated full-platform deployment to hide a missing narrow release path.

questions.prompt: Why can merged lesson JSON remain invisible in the live Academy?
options: The running Auth image still packages the older resources
The browser must create a new identity
questions.explanation: The classpath catalog changes only when the artifact containing it is released.

questions.prompt: Which result proves a protected administrator sees the intended curriculum?
options: An authenticated routed catalog response with the intended version and content
questions.explanation: Source, protection and authenticated runtime visibility are separate gates.

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate deployment scope for an isolated curriculum resource change?
options: Only the verified affected artifact and its necessary checks
A new database and new cluster
questions.explanation: A narrow release reduces risk and preserves unrelated running services.
